question:
A 6-year-old male arrives at the emergency department via ambulance following a motor vehicle
collision. Initial assessment at the scene revealed: unresponsiveness, thready pulses, left tibial
fracture, heart rate 130/min, respiratory rate 29/min, blood pressure 84/51 mm Hg, and Glasgow Coma
Scale score of 10. Left-sided diminished breath sounds, rib deformity, and rightward tracheal deviation
were noted. After failed IV access, an intraosseous (IO) needle was placed in the right anterior
proximal tibia, confirmed by blood aspiration, and normal saline bolus was initiated. Upon ED arrival,
the patient's right calf appears full, pale, and tense. The fluid bolus is discontinued, and the team
prepares for placement of a new IO line. Which of the following locations would be most appropriate for
the next IO insertion? Answer Choices: (A) Left calcaneus (B) Left iliac crest (C) Right proximal
humerus (D) Right calcaneus (E) Sternum (F) Right scapula (G) Left proximal humerus (H) Right distal
femur (I) Right iliac crest (J) Left proximal tibia
 A. Right iliac crest

B. Right distal femur
C. Left proximal tibia
D. Right scapula
E. Left proximal humerus
F. Left calcaneus
G. Right proximal humerus
H. Left iliac crest
I. Sternum
J. Right calcaneus
